THE SIFREI: the heads first, then the people — and 'to the heads of the tribes' teaches that vows are released by experts alone (153:1, R. Yonatan freeing the phrase from Exodus 34:31-32); 'this is the thing' — the husband annuls and the sage permits, neither the other: two a-fortiori refused by the words (153:2); the Sifrei's 152:1 (read at sitting 9, credited) reads 30:1 as punctuation — the frame that closes the calendar. ONKELOS: 'the heads of the tribes', 'this is the word' (cut).

'And a woman, when' three Torah seats — the woman with a discharge (Leviticus 15:19, 15:25) and this; 'in her youth' two Bible seats (30:4, 30:17) — the priest's daughter returns to her father's house 'AS in her youth' (Leviticus 22:13); 'her father's house' seven Bible seats, 'IN her father's house' one; 'and her father is silent to her' the silence-verb's form at 30:5 and 30:8 alone; the stand-root twelve tokens; 'restrains' — the restrain-verb four Torah seats: 30:6, 9, 12 and the spies who 'discouraged' the heart (32:9); 'on the day of his hearing' four seats, all here (30:6, 8, 13, 15) — the hearing-infinitive six tokens, the clock's trigger; 'and the LORD will forgive her' three seats, all in this chapter (30:6, 9, 13), the verb's fourth Bible token Naaman's (2 Kings 5:18); 'her father' six tokens against 'her husband' nine (computed). Yoshiyah) — R. Yonatan: a man's messenger is as himself (153:6).
